title: ClearLedger
problem_statement: Americans aged 25-40 routinely underestimate their monthly spending by 20-35% because subscription charges, automatic renewals, and recurring transfers are spread across 3-5 bank and card accounts with no unified view. Manual budgeting in spreadsheets breaks down within two months for 70% of users (Bankrate 2023), and existing apps like Mint require re-authentication weekly and surface ads rather than actionable guidance. The result is that households exceed self-reported budgets by an average of $312 per month while believing they are on track. A read-only bank-linked ledger that surfaces recurring charges, flags anomalies, and projects month-end balance from actual transaction patterns can close the visibility gap without requiring manual data entry.
target_users: Adults aged 25-40 with 2+ financial accounts who have tried and abandoned spreadsheet budgeting due to maintenance burden
Dual-income households tracking shared expenses across accounts from different banks
Individuals with multiple subscription services who want to audit and cancel recurring charges
First-time earners transitioning from college who have no baseline sense of their monthly spending patterns
user_stories: As a user with accounts at two different banks, I want to see all my transactions in a single chronological feed so that I do not have to log into multiple apps to understand my spending
As a user, I want recurring charges automatically detected and categorized so that I can see exactly how much I spend on subscriptions each month without manually tagging transactions

As a user, I want a month-end balance projection based on my confirmed recurring expenses and historical spending patterns so that I can decide whether I can afford a discretionary purchase before making it
As a user, I want an alert when a subscription charge increases by more than $1 compared to last month so that I catch price hikes from streaming services and SaaS tools immediately
As a user, I want to set a monthly spending limit per category and receive a push notification when I reach 80% of that limit so that I can adjust behavior before the month ends
As a user, I want to see my net worth (assets minus liabilities across all linked accounts) updated daily so that I can track whether I am building or depleting savings over time
As a user who just got paid, I want a one-tap post-paycheck summary showing fixed obligations already deducted and discretionary budget remaining so that I know exactly what I have available to spend
acceptance_criteria: Users can link a checking, savings, or credit card account from any of the 10,000+ US financial institutions supported by Plaid; initial transaction sync covers the trailing 90 days and completes within 3 minutes for accounts with fewer than 500 transactions

Recurring charges are automatically detected within 2 billing cycles; detection accuracy must exceed 90% precision and 85% recall on a labeled test set of 1,000 transactions from beta users before launch

Month-end balance projection is displayed on the home screen and updates within 60 seconds of any new transaction syncing; projection methodology (fixed recurring + 30-day rolling average for variable) is disclosed in a tooltip
Push notifications for category limit alerts (80% and 100% thresholds) are delivered within 10 minutes of the triggering transaction appearing in the feed

Subscription price-change alerts are sent within 24 hours of the anomalous charge posting; alert includes the previous charge amount, new charge amount, and a link to the merchant's cancellation page if available

All financial data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3); the app holds read-only Plaid tokens and cannot initiate transactions; verified by third-party security audit before public launch
The app launches to the home dashboard in under 2 seconds on a mid-range device (iPhone SE 2022, Pixel 6a) with iOS 16 or Android 12 on a cold start
New users complete account linking and see their first unified transaction feed in under 5 minutes; validated with 10 unmoderated usability test participants before App Store submission

success_metrics.metric: D30 retention rate (users who open the app at least once in days 25-30 after install)
success_metrics.baseline: Industry median for personal finance apps: 18% D30 retention (AppsFlyer Finance Benchmark 2023)
success_metrics.target: 28% D30 retention by end of month 3 post-launch, averaged across the first 10,000 installs

success_metrics.metric: Linked accounts per active user (users who opened the app in the trailing 7 days)
success_metrics.baseline: 0 at launch; users with 2+ linked accounts retain at 2.4x the rate of single-account users in comparable apps
success_metrics.target: Average of 2.1 linked accounts per active user within 60 days of launch

success_metrics.metric: Subscription audit completion rate (active users who view the recurring charges screen and cancel or confirm at least one subscription within 14 days of account linking)
success_metrics.baseline: No baseline; metric proxies the core value proposition of finding wasted spend
success_metrics.target: 40% of new users complete a subscription audit within 14 days of linking their first account
Maintain 4.4 stars or above based on at least 500 ratings within 90 days of launch

success_metrics.metric: Weekly notification opt-out rate (users who disable push notifications within 7 days of enabling a budget limit)
success_metrics.baseline: Finance app median opt-out rate: 41% within 30 days (internal estimate from competitor analysis)
success_metrics.target: Notification opt-out rate below 20% within 7 days of first alert, indicating alerts are perceived as useful rather than noisy

risks_open_questions: Plaid connection failures affect 8-12% of bank links on first attempt; need a graceful re-authentication flow and fallback to manual CSV import to avoid losing users at the critical onboarding step

Recurring charge detection based on amount and merchant matching may produce false positives for variable-amount subscriptions (utility bills, usage-based SaaS); need a user correction flow to train the model
Privacy perception risk: users may abandon onboarding when asked for bank credentials via Plaid; need copy and UX testing on consent screens before finalizing onboarding flow
Monetization model not yet validated — freemium with $4.99/month for projections and alerts vs. one-time $9.99 purchase; requires A/B testing with 500+ users before committing to pricing page
iOS App Store review may flag read-only financial data access under guideline 5.1.1; legal and compliance review of App Store submission strategy required 6 weeks before planned launch
How should ClearLedger handle joint accounts shared between partners — should both partners be able to link the same account, and if so, how are budget limits reconciled?
International expansion is out of scope for v1 but Plaid coverage outside the US is limited — if international users discover the app organically, what is the messaging strategy?
out_of_scope: Initiating payments, transfers, or any write access to financial accounts
Tax preparation, tax categorization, or integration with TurboTax or H&R Block at launch
Investment portfolio tracking or brokerage account linking in v1
Shared household budget management with multi-user roles and permissions
Credit score monitoring or credit report integration
International bank account support (US-only at launch via Plaid)
Bill negotiation or cancellation automation on behalf of the user
